concepts.controls: Left / Right or A / D: Slide the boat. Space (hold and release): Lower and reel the hook. Enter: Start / restart.
concepts.core_mechanic: Every friend you catch stays hanging on the hook and becomes part of the pendulum. A jellyfish makes the chain light and floaty, an octopus adds extra swinging tentacles that can grab one more friend, and the whale is so heavy it drags the whole chain into a slow, wide arc — so your best catch can also wreck your next cast. You have to learn the new swing in real time and deliver the whole wobbling chain to your aquarium tank on the dock without bonking it and shaking friends loose.
concepts.juice: Bubble trails stream off the hook, splash rings burst when friends break the surface, and each catch pops with a squash-and-stretch wiggle and a floating "Gotcha!" or "Two in one tow!". A gentle screen sway and a soft "bloop" shake happen when the whale lands, pages of seaweed particles drift up on a perfect delivery, and the aquarium fills with animated friends who follow the hook as it passes. Title screen: the boat bobs under the words FRIEND TOW, with the whale, octopus, and jellyfish already hanging from the hook in a silly, swaying chain.
concepts.lose: Time runs out before the aquarium is full, or you lose too many friends to hard bonks.
concepts.palette: Ocean blues and crayon reds from the drawings, with warm yellow lighthouse light.
concepts.pitch: Cast a swinging hook from your little boat, tow your new sea friends home in a wobbly chain, and fill your aquarium before sunset. The bigger your chain, the wilder it swings — and the whale is a LOT of chain.

roles.role: Your playable boat on the surface. It slides left and right and carries the swinging hook and the aquarium drop-off point on its deck.
The heavyweight star catch. Worth the most room in the aquarium, but catching it makes your pendulum slow, long, and very hard to control.
A living grappling upgrade. While it hangs on the chain, its free tentacles can snag one extra passing friend for a risky double catch.
A floaty wild card. It makes the chain buoyant and bouncy, so it rises faster but bounces off rocks and the lighthouse beam post.

Stands on the dock beside the aquarium. Its slowly rotating beam is your delivery guide — drop the chain into the tank while the beam points at it for a bonus "Perfect Drop" — and its base is a solid obstacle you must not slam your friends into.

concepts.title: Friend Tow
concepts.win: Deliver enough sea friends to fill all 8 spots in the boat's aquarium before the 90-second timer ends.

concepts.controls: Left / Right or A / D: Move the boat along the surface. Space: Cast / reel in time with the lighthouse beat. Enter: Start / restart.
concepts.core_mechanic: The lighthouse beam is your metronome. It sweeps around once per beat, and you can only hook a friend cleanly when you tap Space exactly as the beam crosses your boat — tap early or late and the hook just splashes. As you build a streak, the beam speeds up and starts throwing in half-beats: the whale only surfaces on a big downbeat, the octopus claps two quick tentacle-taps you must match, and jellyfish drift across off-beat to tempt you into breaking your rhythm. Missing a beat doesn't just break your combo — it dims the lighthouse for one sweep, so you have to feel the tempo in the dark.
concepts.juice: Every on-beat tap fires a golden ring from the lighthouse, a musical splash, and a trail of notes and bubbles down the hook line. Combo text pops over the boat — "Nice!", "In the groove!", "Whale of a beat!" — and the caught friends squash, stretch, and then dance in the aquarium in time with the tempo. The screen gives a tiny pulse on each downbeat, the whale's spout shoots heart-shaped spray on a perfect catch, and a missed beat makes the whole scene wobble flat for a moment. Title screen: BEACON BEATS in bouncy letters as the lighthouse beam sweeps across in rhythm, lighting up the whale, octopus, and jellyfish one beat at a time.
concepts.lose: Let your light meter go fully dark by missing too many beats, or finish the song with an incomplete aquarium.
concepts.palette: Deep evening blue water, soft purple jellyfish glow, and warm gold for every on-beat flash.
concepts.pitch: Fish to the beat of a lighthouse in this cozy rhythm game where good timing, not fast hands, fills your aquarium. Keep the groove going as the tempo climbs and the whale, octopus, and jellyfish each demand their own rhythm.

roles.role: Your playable fishing boat. It moves to line up under a friend, then casts only when you tap on the lighthouse beat.
The downbeat boss catch. It only breaches on beat one of a measure, and landing it perfectly fills two aquarium spots.
The double-tap catch. Catching it takes two quick on-beat taps as it claps its tentacles, and once in the aquarium it keeps clapping the tempo for you.
Off-beat tricksters and bonus pickups. They glow on the half-beats — catching one on its exact half-beat extends your combo, but grabbing at one on the main beat breaks it.
The conductor of the whole game. Its rotating beam sets the tempo, shows the beat, and dims or brightens with your performance.

concepts.title: Beacon Beats
concepts.win: Fill all 8 aquarium spots before the 2-minute song ends, keeping the lighthouse lit.

concepts.controls: Left / Right or A / D: Move the boat. Space: Launch the jellyfish / nudge the boat for a tiny bounce-hop. Enter: Start / restart.
concepts.core_mechanic: This is Breakout where the ball is alive. Your jellyfish doesn't just bounce — every time it bonks a friend, that friend grabs its tentacles and rides along, making the jellyfish wider, slower, and droopier. You then have to steer the whole dangling bundle safely back down to the boat's aquarium: bounce them in to unload, or let one more friend pile on for a combo drop and risk the jellyfish getting too heavy and sagging past your boat. The octopus is the prize — it spreads out and turns your jellyfish into a wide, sticky net for one glorious sweep.
concepts.juice: Every bounce leaves a fading purple tentacle trail and a puff of plankton sparkles, friends wiggle and stretch as they grab on, and unloading a bundle bursts into bubbles with combo text like "Bundle of 3!" and "Octo-net!". The boat squashes happily under each delivery, the whale's rescue bounce gives a big soft screen bounce and a spray of droplets, and losing a jellyfish makes a gentle sad "bloop" as it drifts down glowing. Title screen: AQUARIUM BREAKOUT over a calm sea, with the boat bouncing the jellyfish idly beneath the lighthouse while the whale and octopus peek out of bubble blocks.
concepts.lose: Lose all 3 jellyfish past the bottom of the screen before filling the aquarium.
concepts.palette: Bright daytime sea colors straight from the drawings, with glowing purple jellyfish trails.
concepts.pitch: Bounce a friendly jellyfish off bubble blocks to free sea friends, ferry them back to your boat in dangly bundles, and fill your aquarium. Piling on one more friend is always tempting — and always how it all goes sideways.

roles.role: Your paddle. It moves along the bottom, bounces the jellyfish back up, and its deck aquarium is where you unload rescued friends.
A giant, gentle moving bumper near the top. Bouncing off it gives a huge, slow, predictable rebound and it can carry a stuck jellyfish back into play on its spout.
The best bubble-block captive. Freeing it makes your jellyfish sticky and wide for 15 seconds, so friends latch on instead of bouncing off.
Your living ball. It breaks bubble blocks, gathers rescued friends on its tentacles, and gets heavier and wider with every passenger.
A tall, solid wall block on one side of the playfield whose rotating beam periodically nudges drifting bubble blocks sideways, reshuffling the wall mid-game.

concepts.title: Aquarium Breakout
concepts.win: Free and deliver friends to fill all 10 aquarium spots before you run out of jellyfish.
